subject: Dedicated capacity pricing playbook & token-econ next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Tuttle <sara.tuttle@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing playbook & token-econ next steps

Hi Sara — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on pricing/commit and the technical footprint you asked about.

Recap (what we heard)
- Target production workload: low-latency chat + document parsing (mixed prompt lengths, average 450 tokens/session).
- Expected steady-state volume: ~12M tokens/day (peak burst ~2x).
- SLOs: <120ms p50 generation latency, target p95 under 350ms.
- Security: VPC + audit logs required.

Questions we flagged on the call
- Preferred unit economics target: you called out $30–$45 / 1M tokens as an internal target band — confirm if that’s the procurement budget reference.
- GPU preference: you mentioned openness to H100 if price/latency trade-off fits.
- Commitment window: 12–18 month reserved lanes looks likely, but we should confirm flexibility on ramp.

Our preliminary pricing playbook (high-level)
- Reserved dedicated lanes (H100 preferred): 2x H100 reserved as the baseline for initial pilot — modeling shows this meets latency and gives headroom for burst with autoscaling.
- Unit anchor: $36 / 1M tokens (committed monthly minimum tied to reserved lanes).
- Alternative: mixed H100 (inference-optimized) + A100 spot lanes reduces unit cost to ~$28 / 1M at higher latency variance.
- Intro promotion: 10% credit on first three months for pilot customers committing >= 8M tokens/day.

What we need from you to finalize the quote
1) Confirm the procurement budget band (is $30–$45 / 1M tokens authoritative?).
2) Confirm required committed tokens/day for the first 6 months (we used 8–12M/day for modeling).
3) Any hard constraints on GPU brand (must be A100 only / must be H100 allowed).

Next steps
- If budget band confirmed, I’ll share a short workbook with three SKU scenarios (2xH100 reserved; 3xH100 reserved; mixed H100/A100 with burst). Attached draft MAP for the pilot.
- Suggest procurement call with your procurement@orionai.com and our contracts lead next week to lock terms and signature timeline.

Attachments: Orion_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP + objectives), pricing-scenarios-2xH100-vs-mix.xlsx (workbook will follow after you confirm budget).

Thanks — happy to jump on a technical follow-up if Karthik’s team should walk the throughput math next.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Sara Tuttle <sara.tuttle@orionai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orionai.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 18:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing playbook & token-econ next steps

Monica — thanks for the recap and the clear playbook. A few clarifications:

- Budget band: Procurement confirms the team is targeting $25–$40 / 1M tokens for committed, predictable pricing. Engineering would accept higher if the latency/throughput guarantees are rock solid, but procurement will push for a floor around $25.
- Commit horizon: we are comfortable with a 12-month reserved commitment if there are quarterly ramp checkpoints.
- GPU constraint: H100 is preferred for inference perf; procurement wants to see the unit delta vs A100 in the workbook.
- Volume confirmation: we expect to start at ~6M tokens/day for month 1–3, ramping to ~14M tokens/day by month 6.

Procurement asked for: an explicit price per 1M tokens by SKU (2xH100, 3xH100, mixed) and an example invoice math for month 1 vs month 6 given the ramp. Can you include a canary/fallback plan if usage spikes above reserved capacity?

Happy to join the procurement call — I’ll loop procurement@orionai.com into scheduling.

— Sara
Sara Tuttle
Head of Integrations | Orion AI
sara.tuttle@orionai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing playbook & token-econ next steps

Thanks — flagged a couple of tactical items and a proposed anchor to present.

Tactical notes:
- We should present three explicit per-1M anchors: $40 (A100 baseline), $36 (2xH100 reserved), $29 (mixed H100/A100 reserved + burst). Keep $25 as an aspirational discount for a large, longer-term commit.
- Include deterministic invoice examples for 6M/day month 1 and 14M/day month 6. That helps procurement visualize monthly spend ($Xk).
- Add a canary fallback policy in the workbook: 48-hour auto-burst allowed at 1.5x capacity with pre-agreed overage rate (e.g., 1.6x unit price for the burst).

Customer-facing ask:
- If they confirm $25–$40 band, we can push a standard 12-month reserved lanes agreement with flexible quarterly ramp checkpoints.
- Recommend we offer a 6-week SLA review window post-launch where we re-benchmark and adjust lane sizing (no penalty for mutual resizing if traffic profile differs from forecast).

I’ll draft the three-line pricing table and send the workbook back to you before the procurement call.

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 13:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing playbook & token-econ next steps

Quick engineering addendum for the workbook and the call:

- Model performance: on our benchmark (chat model, context 4k, avg gen length 200 tokens), H100 shows ~1.8x sustained throughput vs A100. For Orion’s mixed prompt lengths we should assume 1.5–1.7x in production.
- Sizing: to meet their stated p95 latency target under expected load, 2x H100 is fine for pilot (6–8M/day), but for steady-state 12–14M/day with headroom I recommend 3x H100 reserved or 2x H100 + 2x A100 buffer lanes with autoscale.
- Canary plan: we can provision burst lanes on a different pool and route only flagged customers during initial 2-week ramp to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

I’ll add throughput numbers to the workbook (tokens/sec per GPU with median and p95 rows) so procurement can see the mapping to token-econ.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Tuttle <sara.tuttle@orionai.com>, procurement@orionai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing playbook & token-econ next steps

Sara / Procurement — thanks for the confirmation and the ramp detail. Per internal alignment we’ll deliver the following before the procurement call: 

1) Pricing workbook (attached) showing three SKU scenarios with explicit $ / 1M tokens, invoice math for month 1 (6M/day) and month 6 (14M/day), and canary/fallback overage policy.
2) Proposal language for a 12-month reserved lanes agreement with quarterly ramp checkpoints and a 6-week SLA review clause.
3) A brief technical appendix from Karthik showing tokens/sec per GPU (median/p95) for H100 and A100 under your model profile.

Proposed anchor to discuss on the call: 2x H100 reserved at $36 / 1M tokens, with a mixed-H100 option at $29 / 1M if they opt for a 2xH100 + 2xA100 buffer arrangement and commit >= 12M tokens/day. We’ll also propose a 10% onboarding credit for the first 3 months to accelerate the pilot.

Please let me know availability for a 45-minute procurement + tech sync. I’ll include a preliminary DocuSign link in the workbook for a Letter of Intent so procurement can circulate internally.

Best — Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
